title.rendered: Asleep in the Storm: Why Jesus Could Rest in a Sinking Boat | Living from Rest, Day 6

excerpt.rendered: Jesus slept in a boat the disciples thought was going down. Day 6 of Living from Rest asks what He knew about the storm that we often forget.

content.rendered:
The waves were real. The water was coming in. The disciples were terrified. And Jesus was asleep. Not pretending to sleep. Actually asleep. That is the picture of a life that rests.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, November 6, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 6

Today’s Scripture

“But He was in the stern, asleep on a pillow. And they awoke Him and said to Him, ‘Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?’ Then He arose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, ‘Peace, be still!’ And the wind ceased and there was a great calm.”
Mark 4:38-39 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Mark 4 gives us one of the most quietly extraordinary pictures in all four Gospels. A storm has come up on the Sea of Galilee, the kind that could sink a fishing boat full of seasoned fishermen. The disciples, several of whom made their living on this water, are panicking. And Jesus is at the back of the boat, asleep on a pillow. Mark adds the detail of the pillow. He is not just resting. He is comfortably resting.

Mark 4:38, in the NKJV, says, “But He was in the stern, asleep on a pillow.” The AMPC says, “But He [Himself] was in the stern [of the boat], asleep on the [leather] cushion.” The TPT says, “But Jesus was calmly sleeping in the stern, resting on a cushion.” The scene is set so plainly it is almost absurd. The waves are inside the boat. The men are shouting. The Son of God is sleeping.

How could He rest? Three answers from the text. First, Jesus knew who was in the boat. If He is in the boat, the boat does not go down. The storm will have to go down first. Second, Jesus knew what His Father had said. Earlier that same day, Jesus had said, “Let us cross over to the other side.” If the Father has said to cross, the boat crosses. The storm does not override the word of God. Third, Jesus trusted His Father even when the boat looked like it would sink. Rest and faith are the same muscle.

The disciples wake Him with a question that still rises in our own mouths in a storm: “Do You not care that we are perishing?” It is the honest cry of a believer whose circumstances are shouting louder than the promise. Jesus answers in two steps. First He rebukes the storm. Then He asks the disciples a diagnostic question: “Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?” The faith He is looking for is a resting faith, the kind that sleeps on the back pillow because the Father has already given the word.

So this morning, if your boat is loud, remember who is in the boat with you. The storm is real; so is His authority over it. You are not perishing. He is not asleep because He does not care; He is asleep because He is not worried. And whatever He said to you about this journey still stands. Lie down in the stern beside Him. Rest.

How Jesus Rested in the Storm

He trusted His Father’s word. If God said cross, the boat crosses.

He knew who was in the boat. Presence changes the physics of panic.

He let His authority answer later. He did not need to perform peace; He was peace.

Declaration

Jesus is in the boat with me. The storm is real, but His authority over it is greater. He is not asleep because He does not care; He is at rest because the outcome is secure. I will not panic in this storm. I will rest in the stern with Him, on the pillow of His finished word, until He speaks peace over the wind. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
